papers.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
papers.abstract: Talking-video character replacement requires coordinated transfer of appearance and voice while preserving source motion, scene, and linguistic content. UniSwap presents the first framework for streaming joint audio-visual identity replacement in talking videos using a unified audio-visual diffusion transformer.

papers.title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
papers.abstract: Pose-driven human animation synthesizes video from a reference image and driving pose stream. Real-time generation is essential for interactive applications, yet diffusion-based systems require minutes to hours per clip. LiveAnimate combines real-time streaming with stable long-form generation at billion scale using a 14B-parameter video Diffusion Transformer.

papers.title: An AI4AI Framework for Visual Token Pruning
papers.abstract: AutoPrune uses large language models to automatically design visual-token pruning policies for multimodal models via a domain-specific language. The framework achieves high efficiency by removing 94.4% of visual tokens while preserving 99% of full-token performance and reducing FLOPs by 9.9x.

papers.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
papers.abstract: H2R-Bench evaluates cross-embodiment human-to-robot manipulation video generation, transforming egocentric human demonstrations into robot manipulation videos. The benchmark evaluates generated videos across five dimensions including goal-state completion, action-event completion, and embodiment correctness.

papers.title: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: HPSE improves unstructured knowledge editing by distilling from hybrid rollouts that insert missing facts into the model's reasoning paths. This enables composable multi-hop reasoning without external supervision, establishing plug-and-play improvements across four LLM backbones and two knowledge editors.

papers.title: SKILLER: Language-Level Reinforcement Learning for Reusable Skill Extraction in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: SKILLER automatically generates executor-specific skills for small models using natural-language-driven reinforcement learning. The framework employs a strong model as actor and critic, achieving absolute gains from 4.3 to 20.4 percentage points for the 9B model while matching closed-source performance.

papers.title: Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation
papers.abstract: CMD aligns teacher supervision with causal generation context for few-step autoregressive video models. By matching temporal information boundaries and evaluation context, the framework improves control adherence and long-video quality, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks.

papers.title: Knowing When to Quit: Diagnosing and Training LLMs to Abort Futile Reasoning
papers.abstract: CaRL uses reinforcement learning with refusal incentives to reduce futile reasoning in LLMs while preserving task performance. The approach aligns model behavior with capability boundaries, substantially reducing plausible-sounding but incorrect derivations on beyond-capability tasks.

papers.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity
papers.abstract: This study examines how instruction tuning affects model confidence and rationale diversity in question-answering tasks. Findings show instruction tuning consistently alters answer confidence and reduces cross-rationale diversity without improving likelihood-based calibration or predictive accuracy.

papers.title: From Inaudible Inputs to Model Failures: Low-Frequency Safety Risks in LALMs
papers.abstract: Researchers propose ILL, a black-box red-teaming method using inaudible low-frequency waveforms to expose audio-language model vulnerabilities. DRG defense detects distribution shifts and requests reacquisition, raising mean attacked accuracy from 28.5% to 46.1% after clean rerecording.

cc_updates.body: Subagent forking is now on by default: a `subagent_type: "fork"` subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache, and non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now run in the background by default. Type `@` in the prompt to mention another Claude session by name; Claude then uses `SendMessage` to reach that session directly. `SendMessage` now delivers to a bare name that exactly matches one live session, instead of asking to confirm with a ref first. Interactive sessions on one machine now keep unique names: starting or renaming a session to a name another live session already uses gives it a `name-word-word` variant and tells you. Added `/config` rows for "Dialog expiry" and "Messages from your other sessions" (cross-session inbound accept/hold/refuse). Added secret redaction for GitLab token families and full redaction of routable tokens; the `glab` CLI config store gets the same sandbox and credential-path protection as `gh`. Added GitLab support to plugin marketplaces: bare `gitlab.com` repo URLs now clone like `github.com` URLs.
Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in failing with a redirect URI mismatch for servers that use a pre-registered OAuth client, such as Slack

Documented `claude remote-control --continue` for resuming the most recent Remote Control session. Added server-supplied Claude Code hook support for self-hosted runner sessions, matching managed-environment behavior. Added SSE keepalive pings to gateway streaming responses during long thinking pauses, preventing idle-timeout disconnects on Vertex and Bedrock upstreams. Added plugin marketplace `command` sources: a local command (e.g. an IDE) prints the plugin directory, which is re-resolved each session and applied without a restart; `mode: "link"` uses it in place. `ListAgents` now marks disconnected Remote Control sessions as `offline` and labels your cloud sessions as `cloud`. Fixed long responses partly disappearing while streaming and being printed twice in the terminal.
